transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I start projects excited, but I just can’t seem to follow through and finish assignments or client work on time unless there’s a crisis. It's gotten to the point where it's really starting to affect my classes and my freelance work, and I realized I need some help.
Do you also often feel physically restless or impulsive, like you can’t sit still, interrupt others, or act before thinking?

Yes, definitely—I often feel this buzzing under my skin when I have to sit still, so I'm constantly bouncing my leg, pacing, or finding things to do because I just can't chill. I also struggle with impulsivity and constantly catch myself interrupting or cutting people off during group projects before they can even finish their sentences, which I always feel terrible about afterward.
Did these attention, restlessness, and impulsive symptoms start before age 12, and were they also present in more than one setting such as home and school?

Yes, they definitely go back to elementary school. My teachers always commented that I was bright but daydreamed, rushed, and blurted out answers, and my parents got called in because I'd constantly fidget and forget to hand in homework I'd actually finished. It was definitely a constant issue both at school and at home.
Have you also had ongoing problems with breaking rules, getting into fights, lying, stealing, destroying property, or getting suspended or expelled from school?

No, I've never had any issues like that at all. I've never gotten into fights, stolen anything, or destroyed property, and I was never suspended or expelled from school. My struggles have always been about focus, restlessness, and disorganization, rather than breaking rules.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a longstanding childhood-onset pattern of inattention, hyperactivity/restlessness, and impulsivity occurring in multiple settings (home and school), with clear functional impairment in classes and freelance work. There is no history of conduct problems, supporting ADHD, predominantly inattentive/combined presentation within ICD-10 code F90.0.
